name: Vitamin D3 + K2

info.does: Vitamin D supports bones, muscles and immune function. Above about 40° N your skin makes very little from October to April. K2 (MK-7) helps direct calcium into bone.
info.research: Strong evidence that supplements correct low vitamin D status. Benefits for energy and mood show up mainly in people who start low.
info.how: With a meal that has some fat (eggs, yogurt, nut butter).
info.side: Rare at standard doses. Don't add another vitamin D product without checking the total.
info.interacts: K2 can change how warfarin works.

source: NIH ODS Vitamin D fact sheet; Health Canada monograph: Vitamin D

name: Vitamin D3

info.does: Vitamin D supports bones, muscles and immune function, and most people make little of it in winter.
info.research: Strong evidence that supplements correct low vitamin D status.
info.how: With a meal that has some fat.

source: NIH ODS Vitamin D fact sheet

name: Algae omega-3

info.does: EPA and DHA support heart, brain and joint health. Algae is where fish get theirs, so it suits vegetarians.
info.research: Moderate: modest drops in exercise soreness and joint stiffness, small mood benefits, and reliable effects on triglycerides.
info.how: With a meal to avoid aftertaste.
info.side: Mild stomach upset in some people.
info.interacts: High doses can add to blood thinners.

source: NIH ODS Omega-3 Fatty Acids fact sheet

name: Fish oil omega-3

info.does: EPA and DHA support heart, brain and joint health.
info.research: Moderate to strong depending on the outcome; reliable effects on triglycerides.
info.how: With a meal to avoid fishy aftertaste.
info.interacts: High doses can add to blood thinners.

source: NIH ODS Omega-3 Fatty Acids fact sheet

name: Creatine monohydrate

info.does: Tops up creatine stores in muscle and brain. Vegetarians start lower, so they tend to respond more.
info.research: Strong for strength and repeated-effort performance. Emerging evidence for thinking and focus after short sleep.
info.how: In any drink, any time of day. Taking it every day matters more than timing.
info.side: About 0.5–1 kg of water weight in muscle in the first weeks.
info.interacts: Check with a doctor first if you have kidney disease.

source: ISSN position stand: creatine supplementation (Kreider et al., 2017)

name: Vitamin B12

info.does: B12 is needed for red blood cells and nerves. Plant-based diets supply little of it, and stores run down slowly over years.
info.research: Strong: people who eat little or no meat often have low B12, and supplements reliably raise it.
info.how: Your body absorbs a small share of each dose, so three days a week is enough at 1,000 mcg.
info.side: Very rare. Your body clears what it doesn't use.
info.interacts: Metformin and acid reducers lower B12.

source: NIH ODS Vitamin B12 fact sheet

info.does: Magnesium helps muscles relax and calms the nervous system. Hard training and some medicines can lower your levels.
info.research: Moderate: small improvements in falling asleep, mainly in people who get too little. The glycinate form is gentle on the stomach.
info.how: In warm water 60–90 minutes before bed.
info.side: Loose stools at higher doses. Glycinate is the gentlest form.
info.interacts: Keep 4 hours away from thyroid medicine and 2 hours from iron and some antibiotics.

name: Ashwagandha

info.does: A root extract that may lower stress hormones and how stressed you feel.
info.research: Moderate: several randomised trials of KSM-66 show lower stress scores and faster sleep onset over 8 weeks.
info.how: With dinner. 8 weeks on, then 2 weeks off.
info.side: Drowsiness or stomach upset. Rare liver injury reports: stop and see a doctor if you notice yellowing skin or dark urine.
info.interacts: Thyroid medicine, sedatives and immune suppressants. Not for pregnancy.

source: Health Canada NHP monograph: Ashwagandha; Chandrasekhar et al., 2012

name: Curcumin

info.does: The active compound in turmeric. It may ease soreness and inflammation after hard training.
info.research: Moderate: small trials show less muscle soreness and knee discomfort. Plain turmeric is poorly absorbed, so an enhanced form is used.
info.side: Stomach upset. Rare liver reports with high-absorption forms.

source: NIH NCCIH Turmeric; Health Canada NHP monograph: Turmeric

name: Iron bisglycinate

requires_lab.reason: Too much iron is harmful, and only a blood test can tell whether you need it.

info.does: Rebuilds iron stores when a blood test shows they are low.
info.research: Strong when ferritin is low. Every other day is absorbed as well as daily and is easier on the stomach.
info.how: With vitamin C food, 2 hours away from coffee, tea and dairy.
info.side: Constipation or stomach upset. Bisglycinate is the gentlest form.
info.interacts: Separate from magnesium, zinc and calcium by 2 hours and from thyroid medicine by 4 hours.

source: NIH ODS Iron fact sheet; Stoffel et al., 2017 (alternate-day dosing)

name: Melatonin

info.does: A hormone that signals night-time to your body clock.
info.research: Moderate for shifting a late body clock and jet lag; weak for general insomnia.
info.how: A low dose 30–60 minutes before bed.

source: NIH NCCIH Melatonin; Health Canada NHP monograph: Melatonin

info.does: A herb sometimes used for low mood.
info.research: Moderate for mild low mood, but it interacts with many medicines.
info.interacts: Birth control, antidepressants, blood thinners and many other medicines.

info.does: Protein from animal connective tissue, used for joints and skin.
info.research: Emerging: small trials on joint comfort in athletes and skin elasticity.

info.does: An amino acid from tea that may take the edge off a busy mind.
info.research: Emerging: small trials on relaxation and sleep quality.

info.does: An amino acid that may help you feel more rested after sleep.
info.research: Emerging: small trials on subjective sleep quality.

name: Vitamin C

info.does: Supports immune function and helps absorb plant iron.
info.research: Moderate: regular use slightly shortens colds; it doesn't prevent them in most people.

source: NIH ODS Vitamin C fact sheet; Cochrane review (Hemilä & Chalker, 2013)

info.research: Emerging to moderate for immune support when intake is low.
info.side: Nausea on an empty stomach. Long-term high doses lower copper.
info.interacts: Space 2 hours from iron and some antibiotics.

name: Folate

info.does: Folate is needed for healthy cell growth and is recommended before and during pregnancy.
info.research: Strong: folic acid before conception lowers neural tube defect risk.
info.how: With breakfast, ideally inside a prenatal vitamin your care provider approves.

source: Health Canada: Folic acid and neural tube defects; NIH ODS Folate fact sheet

requires_lab.reason: Iodine affects the thyroid, so we only add it with your care provider's input.

info.does: Needed to make thyroid hormone; needs rise in pregnancy.
info.research: Strong for preventing deficiency; too much can also upset the thyroid.
